title: Stable duplicated invariant is an abstraction opportunity
task: Review the same normalization and validation invariant duplicated across several independent callers.
context: Five callers normalize identifiers using the same algorithm.
The invariant has been stable for a year.
Changes to the rule must be applied consistently everywhere.
Past bugs came from one caller missing an update.
The logic does not depend on caller-specific mode flags.
evidence: Repository history shows three synchronized edits to all five copies.
The same edge cases and error semantics are required in every caller.
A shared pure function/module can express the invariant without caller-specific branches.
snippet: normalize -> validate checksum -> canonicalize case  # copied in five callers
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep duplication forever because abstraction is risky.
Treat every duplicated block as independent despite synchronized changes.
Build a generic framework instead of a small invariant-focused abstraction.
expected_decision_properties: Recommend centralizing the stable shared invariant.
Use the smallest abstraction that expresses the common rule.
Identify synchronized change history and divergence bugs as evidence.
Avoid expanding the abstraction to unrelated caller-specific behavior.
unacceptable_reasoning: Duplication is always safer than abstraction.
Any abstraction requires a framework or interface hierarchy.
Repeated synchronized changes are irrelevant evidence.
verification_expectations: Add shared invariant tests covering all known edge cases.
Run caller-level regression tests after centralization.
Verify no caller-specific semantics were accidentally absorbed.
revisit_when: Caller semantics diverge enough that the shared abstraction requires mode flags or caller-specific branches.
